turns.en: Here are your tablets for this morning. Have you got some water there? Just the two white ones now, the other one's after lunch.
turns.cy: Dyma'ch tabledi chi ar gyfer bore 'ma. Oes gynnoch chi ddŵr yn fan'na? Dim ond y ddwy wen rŵan — mae'r llall ar ôl cinio.
chunks: Here are your tablets for this morning
Dyma'ch tabledi chi ar gyfer bore 'ma
Have you got some water there?
Oes gynnoch chi ddŵr yn fan'na?
possession relocates to the existential with conjugated gan; 'some' erases inside it
Just the two white ones now
Dim ond y ddwy wen rŵan
restrictive 'just' → dim ond, kept apart from the erased softener and from jyst; tabled is feminine, hence dwy + gwen→wen

turns.en: Righto. I've still got the water from breakfast here.
turns.cy: Reit-o. Mae gen i'r dŵr o frecwast yn fan'ma o hyd.
chunks: I've still got the water from breakfast here
Mae gen i'r dŵr o frecwast yn fan'ma o hyd
the mae gen i possessive; 'still' lands clause-finally as o hyd
south: mae … gyda fi — AND A REORDER
turns.southLine: Reit-o. Mae'r dŵr o frecwast gyda fi fan hyn o hyd.

turns.en: Perfect. Let me just watch you take those, and then I can sign them off.
turns.cy: Perffaith. Gadwch i mi jyst eich gwylio chi'n eu cymryd nhw, ac wedyn mi fedra i'w cofnodi nhw.
chunks: Let me just watch you take those
Gadwch i mi jyst eich gwylio chi'n eu cymryd nhw
gadwch i mi (R3); the stacked possessive objects eich…chi and eu…nhw
and then I can sign them off
ac wedyn mi fedra i'w cofnodi nhw
sequential 'then' → wedyn (S1); English's particle verb 'sign off' becomes the single verb cofnodi

turns.en: There. All gone. You can tick your box.
turns.cy: Dyna fo. Wedi mynd i gyd. Mi gewch chi roi tic yn eich bocs.
chunks: distinct from 'There we are' → Dyna ni
Mi gewch chi roi tic yn eich bocs
English's denominal verb 'to tick' has no Welsh reflex — rhoi tic, 'put a tick'

turns.en: Lovely. I'll be back with the after-lunch one, so don't take anything in the meantime.
turns.cy: Hyfryd. Mi fydda i'n ôl efo'r un ar-ôl-cinio, felly peidiwch â chymryd dim byd yn y cyfamser.
chunks: I'll be back with the after-lunch one
Mi fydda i'n ôl efo'r un ar-ôl-cinio
so don't take anything in the meantime
felly peidiwch â chymryd dim byd yn y cyfamser
'anything' under a negative imperative → dim byd; the any/some distinction erases

turns.cy: Dallt. Mi arhosa i amdanoch chi.
chunks: English's bare passive participle has no Welsh reflex — the verbal noun stands alone
aros governs am, conjugated as amdanoch chi

turns.en: Here are your tablets. Just the two white ones now, the other's after lunch.
turns.cy: Dyma'ch tabledi chi. Dim ond y ddwy wen rŵan — mae'r llall ar ôl cinio.
chunks: Just the two white ones now
Dim ond y ddwy wen rŵan
converges with 'the other one's after lunch' — reception, welcome

turns.en: What's this new one for? I don't recognise it.
turns.cy: I be mae'r un newydd 'ma? Dw i ddim yn ei nabod hi.
chunks: the same purpose-cleft head as 'that's what the bell's for' (R3), turned into a question
Dw i ddim yn ei nabod hi
nabod for acquaintance-knowing, against gwybod for facts (S5); feminine hi for the tablet

turns.en: That's the new one the doctor started yesterday - for your blood pressure. It's instead of the old blue one, not as well as.
turns.cy: Dyna'r un newydd ddechreuodd y doctor ddoe — ar gyfer eich pwysau gwaed chi. Mae hi yn lle'r hen un las, nid yn ogystal â hi.
chunks: That's the new one the doctor started yesterday
Dyna'r un newydd ddechreuodd y doctor ddoe
the object relative takes a bare mutated verb — no relative pronoun at all
ar gyfer eich pwysau gwaed chi
It's instead of the old blue one, not as well as
Mae hi yn lle'r hen un las, nid yn ogystal â hi
English strands 'as well as'; Welsh must restate the pronoun, so the gapping does not survive

turns.en: Instead of, not as well as. Got it. There's a lot to keep track of, isn't there?
turns.cy: Yn lle, nid yn ogystal â. Dallt. Mae 'na lot i'w gofio, does?
chunks: Instead of, not as well as
Yn lle, nid yn ogystal â
as 'Understood' — one form for the ratifying intention
There's a lot to keep track of
English's tracking metaphor has no Welsh reflex; cofio carries it
the verb-echo tag system — Welsh tags with the verb, never with a pronoun

turns.en: There is, and you keep asking every time - you're the best safety check we've got.
turns.cy: Oes, ac mi dach chi'n dal i ofyn bob tro — chi ydy'r tsiec diogelwch gorau sy gynnon ni.
chunks: the verb-echo answer — Welsh answers an existential with its own verb
and you keep asking every time
ac mi dach chi'n dal i ofyn bob tro
you're the best safety check we've got
chi ydy'r tsiec diogelwch gorau sy gynnon ni
identificatory fronting; possession as the relative sy gynnon ni

turns.en: Well! Nobody's ever called me that before.
turns.cy: Wel! Does neb erioed wedi fy ngalw i'n hynny o'r blaen.
chunks: Nobody's ever called me that before
Does neb erioed wedi fy ngalw i'n hynny o'r blaen
Welsh negative concord: the existential negative carries neb and erioed together, where English has one negative

turns.en: Here are your tablets for this morning - the two white ones now.
turns.cy: Dyma'ch tabledi chi ar gyfer bore 'ma — y ddwy wen rŵan.
chunks: Here are your tablets for this morning
Dyma'ch tabledi chi ar gyfer bore 'ma

turns.en: I don't think these are mine. I usually have three.
turns.cy: Dw i ddim yn meddwl mai fi pia'r rhain. Dw i'n cael tair fel arfer.
chunks: I don't think these are mine
Dw i ddim yn meddwl mai fi pia'r rhain
⚠ line — the mai-cleft under a negated matrix, and Welsh's piau possessive predicate
Dw i'n cael tair fel arfer
⚠ line — feminine tair, agreeing with tabled; 'usually' lands clause-finally

turns.en: Then let's stop right there and check - you're quite right to say. Can you tell me your full name and date of birth?
turns.cy: Dewch i ni stopio'n fan'na 'ta, a tsiecio — dach chi'n hollol iawn i ddeud. Fedrwch chi ddeud eich enw llawn a'ch dyddiad geni wrtha i?

turns.en: Margaret Hughes, third of March, forty-one. It's the tablets I don't recognise, see.
turns.cy: Margaret Hughes, y trydydd o Fawrth, pedwar deg un. Y tabledi dw i ddim yn eu nabod, ylwch.
chunks: Margaret Hughes, third of March, forty-one
Margaret Hughes, y trydydd o Fawrth, pedwar deg un
⚠ line — the clipped year read as a bare decimal number (R5)
It's the tablets I don't recognise
Y tabledi dw i ddim yn eu nabod
⚠ line — the focus cleft; Welsh fronts without any dummy 'it is'

turns.en: Thank you for saying. I'll double-check the chart with the pharmacist right now, and I won't give you anything until we're certain.
turns.cy: Diolch am ddeud. Mi wna i tsiecio'r siart ddwywaith efo'r fferyllydd rŵan, a wna i ddim rhoi dim byd i chi nes byddwn ni'n siŵr.
chunks: I'll double-check the chart with the pharmacist right now
Mi wna i tsiecio'r siart ddwywaith efo'r fferyllydd rŵan
⚠ line — English's prefix 'double-' relocates to the adverb ddwywaith, keeping the one tsiec- lexeme (R7)

a wna i ddim rhoi dim byd i chi nes byddwn ni'n siŵr
⚠ line — the nes clause takes the future, where English uses a present

turns.en: Better safe than sorry, my mother always said.
turns.cy: Gwell diogel nag edifar, medda fy mam i bob amser.
